guidelines.detail: general guideline covering EXS-007 (example 02) and this example

refines ACT-05 (The reference models the post-resolution feedback as the task "Provide feedback" (M1), while the generated model uses an intermediate catch event "Satisfaction feedback received" (X1). The description (S6) states only that customers can provide feedback after resolution, with no wait for a message, signal, time or condition. The generator therefore chose the wrong BPMN element type, which is the s)

new guideline (The generated model omits the flow from the notification task to the reimbursement task (F2), and the reference places the notification before the split on the refund outcome (M5, M1). The documented guidelines do not cover a notification step between a decision and a conditional follow-up. The closest learned guideline, LRN-027, says to place the gateway directly after the review without a separa)

refines GW-01 (The generated model folded the outcome decision into the review task label (P3) and into the notification label (P6). It therefore has no exclusive gateway after the review (M4) and no separate rejection task (M2), so the labels diverge from the reference. The guideline makes the decision a gateway and keeps the task labels to the action performed, which removes the label divergence and the missin)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that, after a decision or condition, one outcome requires an extra activity before the process continues, while the other outcome skips that activity, and both outcomes then lead to the same later step: Model an exclusive gateway at the decision point with one outgoing flow to the extra activity under the condition where it applies and a second outgoing flow under the complementary condition that bypasses it. Connect the end of the extra activity and the bypass flow into one merging exclusive gateway, and connect that merge to the shared later step. Do not connect the extra activity directly to the shared later step, and do not omit the bypass branch.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that, after a decision or condition, one outcome requires an extra activity before the process continues, while the other outcome skips that activity, and both outcomes then lead to the same later step
rules_sent_back.source: learned guideline (refines GW-03), generalized from EXS-007

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that an external participant performs an action as a regular step after an earlier step, and no waiting for a message, signal, time or condition is described for that action: Model that action as a bpmn:task placed in sequence after the preceding step. Do not model it as an intermediate catch event, because a catch event represents a wait for an occurrence and is only appropriate when the description explicitly describes such a wait.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that an external participant performs an action as a regular step after an earlier step, and no waiting for a message, signal, time or condition is described for that action

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that an outcome is communicated to a party by a notification action, and a conditional follow-up action then depends on that outcome: Model the notification action as its own task placed in sequence before the exclusive gateway that routes to the conditional follow-up. Connect the notification task to the gateway, and connect the gateway's branch for the positive outcome to the follow-up task, so the routing follows the notification and the follow-up is not left unconnected to it. Keep a separate bypass branch for the other outcome, as the description states.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that an outcome is communicated to a party by a notification action, and a conditional follow-up action then depends on that outcome

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that an assessment or review is followed by an outcome-dependent condition (for example 'if approved') that decides whether a later activity is carried out, and it does not describe the approval as a separate piece of work: Model an exclusive gateway directly after the review or assessment task, with one conditioned outgoing flow for each outcome. Connect the positive outcome to the activity that depends on it. Do not insert a separate approval task between the review and the gateway, so the gateway is the decision point that governs the next activity.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a determination with two possible outcomes is communicated to a party, that the negative outcome has its own separately described action, and that the outcome-dependent branches continue to a common later step

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that one step both performs work on an item and decides which of two or more outcomes applies, and each outcome leads to a different follow-up action: Model the work step as a task whose label names only the action performed. Keep the outcome terms out of that label. Place an exclusive gateway after the task, with one conditioned outgoing flow per outcome. Give each outcome its own task for the follow-up action it requires, and do not use one generic task that covers both the decision and its consequence.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that one step both performs work on an item and decides which of two or more outcomes applies, and each outcome leads to a different follow-up action
